title: "Reference: initialization and classes"
---

The reference has four parts: **[1 · Initialization and classes](api.qmd)** · [2 · Solvers](solvers.qmd) · [3 · Getters and saved results](reference/getters.qmd) · [4 · Plot functions](reference/plots.qmd).

`PRESS` represents **one match**. Input conversion, navigation, numerical inference, result storage and plotting are separate operations. Initialization copies and validates the supplied tables; it does not run models. The five fitted models are shipped with the package and load lazily, without training.

## Initialization

```python
from PRESS import PRESS

press = PRESS(
    tracking_data,
    events_data=None,
    *,
    possessions_data=None,
    player_possessions_data=None,
    actions_data=None,
    fps=10.0,
    pitch_length=None,
    pitch_width=None,
    match_id=None,
    player_metadata=None,
    ball_drive_model=None,
    pass_risk_model=None,
    pass_selection_model=None,
    action_selection_model=None,
    residual_risk_model=None,
)
```

All arguments after `events_data` are keyword-only. Each model argument accepts a fitted model instance, its JSON-manifest path, or `None` for the installed pretrained model.

### Canonical tracking contract

Positions are **centred pitch metres**; x spans `[-length/2, length/2]` and y spans `[-width/2, width/2]`. Velocities are m/s in those same axes. Data from a provider with another origin, scale or orientation must be converted first. No smoothing, interpolation, resampling or velocity estimation occurs implicitly.

| Input | Required information |
|---|---|
| `tracking_data` | Wide DataFrame, one row per unique integer `frame`; `ball_x`, `ball_y`, `player_possession`, `attacking_side`; player columns `<player_id>_x`, `_y`, `_vx`, `_vy`. |
| Player IDs | Internal aliases `home_<integer>` / `away_<integer>`. The integer is an identifier and need not be a shirt number. The carrier must name a player with tracking columns. |
| Optional speed | `<player_id>_v` is derived as `hypot(vx,vy)` only when absent. Supplied components are not re-estimated. |
| Carrier and direction | Carrier can be missing in flight/no-control frames. Model evaluation needs an observed carrier and `left_to_right` or `right_to_left`. A plain frame plot also supports missing carriers. |
| Missing players | Missing XY observations can remain missing; physical states pad absent players internally. An observed player requires finite velocity. More than eleven observed players on a team is rejected. |
| `fps` | Actual input frequency in Hz, default 10. Consecutive integer frame IDs are sampling ticks; missing observations retain their original IDs. This is independent of the numerical solver steps. |
| Pitch dimensions | Explicit positive metre values, or constant `pitch_length` / `pitch_width` columns. If neither is supplied, defaults are 105 × 68 m. Conflicting explicit/input dimensions raise `ValueError`. |
| `match_id` | Optional match identifier, inferred from a single-valued tracking column if present. Multiple matches are rejected. |
| `player_metadata` | Optional roster keyed by unique internal `player_id`; may retain source IDs and names. |

Observed player velocities containing NaN or infinity are rejected. Missing players are not replaced with estimated positions. Large coordinates used for internal padding are excluded from pressure-line calculations and plots.

### Possessions, actions and context

| Table | Schema and purpose |
|---|---|
| `possessions_data` | Explicit **team** intervals: unique `possession_id`, `team_id` (`home`/`away`), inclusive integer `frame_start`, `frame_end`. Optional `lost` supports reporting. Team intervals cannot overlap. |
| `player_possessions_data` | Alternative **individual** intervals, linked through verified successful passes. See the linking contract below. Do not supply both individual and team interval tables. |
| `actions_data` | Inclusive intervals with `frame_start`, `frame_end`, `action`, `start_type`, `previous_action`. Optional `possession_id`, `is_canonical`, `time_since_start` and other annotations retain their meaning. The package does not invent a segmentation; the conventions are in [Possession segmentation and context](vignettes/setup/possession_and_checkpoint_setup.ipynb). |
| `events_data` | Optional canonical events with `frame`, `player_id`, `team_id`, `event_type`. Pass events additionally require boolean `is_successful` and an identified receiver for completions. Raw provider events must be adapted first. |

Team possession and individual control are distinct. A completed pass can link two individual intervals inside one team possession. Neither table is inferred from carrier changes alone. Frame-level computation does not require either table when its necessary context is supplied explicitly.

The individual linking helper is `PRESS.utils.match.link_team_possessions(player_possessions)`. It requires `player_id`, `frame_start`, `frame_end`, `end_type`, `pass_outcome`, `target_pass`, `frame_receipt` and boolean `loss`; `possession_id` enables individual-ID getters. Optional `period` and `game_interruption_after` prevent linking across periods/stoppages. It returns copied `(team_intervals, player_intervals_with_team_possession_id)`. Intervals cannot overlap. A successful link requires the same team, an identified matching recipient, reception at the next interval's start and no recorded interruption.

Current-state context may include `start_type_raw`, `previous_action_raw`, `match_clock_min` and `score_difference_prefix`. Future destinations, outcomes, remaining duration and final score are not context inputs. Individual elapsed time and completed one-second carries (`completed_canonical_drives`) are derived from annotated starts using `fps`. An unknown elapsed time is never imputed to zero.

## Data from another provider

```python
press = PRESS.from_long(
    players, ball, context,
    home_team=home_team_id,
    away_team=away_team_id,
    fps=input_frequency,
    pitch_length=length_metres,
    pitch_width=width_metres,
    match_id=match_id,
)
```

The adapter takes three DataFrames from one match:

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `players` | `frame`, source `team_id`, source `player_id`, `x`, `y`, `vx`, `vy`; one observation per player/frame. Missing players may be omitted. |
| `ball` | `frame`, `x`, `y`; optional `z`, `vx`, `vy`, `vz`. One row per context frame. |
| `context` | `frame`, source `player_possession`, `attacking_side`; optional clock, score and action context. Missing carrier is allowed. Add source `team_possession` when player IDs repeat across teams. |

Rename provider columns and convert units/axes **before** calling this adapter. Home/away source IDs are explicit. Internal aliases follow first appearance within each team; the original mapping is returned by `press.get_players()`. Optional interval/event tables supplied to `from_long` also use source IDs and are remapped consistently. `PRESS.io.tracking_from_long(...)` exposes the same conversion separately, returning `(wide_tracking, roster)`.

The adapter provides a common data format, not validation of the pretrained models on another league or provider. Event categories should be mapped to equivalent meanings where possible; the saved tree-model vocabularies otherwise use their missing/unseen buckets.

## Processed SkillCorner files

```python
press = PRESS.from_skillcorner(match_dir, actions_path=actions_path)
```

`match_dir` contains `<match_id>_tracking.parquet` and `<match_id>_possession.parquet` from this project's preprocessing (see [the annotated input tables](data.qmd#input-tables)). The optional CSV/parquet actions table is filtered to that match. The default input frequency is 10 Hz; additional constructor keywords can select models or metadata. Reading parquet requires the `io` extra. This method does not preprocess raw SkillCorner files.

## Main classes

| Class | Role and public entry points |
|---|---|
| `PRESS` | One-match facade. Computes and stores components through the [solver methods](solvers.qmd), navigates annotations through [getters](reference/getters.qmd), and saves/restores results. |
| `MatchInfo` | Immutable `fps`, `pitch_length`, `pitch_width`, optional `match_id`. `to_dict()` returns copied metadata. |
| `BallDriveModel` | Frozen physical/spline model. `pretrained()`, `from_json(path)`, `to_dict()`, `predict(...)`, `predict_batch(...)`. |
| `PassRiskModel` | Frozen trajectory-MLE parameters and isotonic map. `pretrained()`, `from_json(path)`, `to_dict()`, `calibrate(p)`, `predict_field(...)`, `predict_from_times(...)`. |
| `PassSelectionModel` | Frozen categorical destination-choice model. `pretrained()`, `from_json(path)`, `to_dict()`, `build_features(...)`, `predict_features(...)`. |
| `ActionSelectionModel` | Native binary pass/carry policy. `pretrained()`, `from_json(path)`, `to_dict()`, `build_feature_record(...)`, `build_features(...)`, `encode(...)`, `predict_features(...)`. |
| `ResidualRiskModel` | Conditional terminal individual loss after a successful carry. Same artifact readers, `features_from_action_record(...)`, `build_features(...)`, `encode(...)`, `predict_features(...)`. |
| `BCOS` | Optional standalone spatial descriptor, imported from `PRESS.extras`. `compute_bcos(...)` and `get_result(...)`; alternatively use `press.compute_bcos(...)` to keep its output in the match cache. |

Import fitted classes from `PRESS.model`. Tree readers validate their adjacent UBJ checksum, vocabulary and feature order. JSON and UBJ files are the pretrained models, not benchmark fit-output directories. Physical scales, calibration maps and xT surfaces come from the supplied artifact; initialization does not re-estimate them.

### Standalone model array contracts

| Method | Input → output |
|---|---|
| `BallDriveModel.predict(r_defs, v_defs, x_bc, v_bc, *, horizon=1, physics_kwargs=None)` | Defender positions/velocities `(D,2)`, carrier `(2,)` → loss, survival, defender causes, times and metadata. `predict_batch` adds a leading state dimension. |
| `PassRiskModel.predict_field(p_pos, p_vel, x_bc, targets, attacker_idx, ball_carrier_idx, *, physics_kwargs=None)` | Players `(P,2)`, targets `(M,2)` → player control `(P,M)`, raw/calibrated attacking completion, flight times and metadata. |
| `PassSelectionModel.build_features(**state)` | Current state and target-wise raw control → full candidate feature matrix. `predict_features(matrix, *, log_membership=None, calibrated=True)` returns normalized destination probabilities. |
| `ActionSelectionModel.build_feature_record(**state)` | Current carrier/players, grid, destination choices, **calibrated** pass completion, drive loss (converted once to the `drive_success_1s` feature), BCOS and context → one feature dictionary. `build_features` encodes it; `predict_features` returns native P(pass). |
| `ResidualRiskModel.features_from_action_record(record, *, time_since_start, action_model)` | Current action record, observed elapsed time and matching action model → residual feature matrix, including native P(carry). `predict_features` returns terminal loss probability conditional on a successful carry. |

The full state keyword contract of the two tree feature builders is documented in their Python docstrings and the [action-selection model vignette](vignettes/04_action_selection/04_action_selection.ipynb). Contextual names and feature polarity retain their trained meaning: pass selection uses raw control and **drive loss**; action selection uses calibrated completion and **drive success**. Residual risk reuses the drive success of the action-selection record, and the composition of h and xLoss uses drive loss.

## Package layout

```text
PRESS/
  core/           match initialization, navigation, orchestration and result access
  io/             explicit input adapters, validation and JSON/NPZ result exports
  model/          fitted inference classes, feature builders and numerical solvers
  physics/        motion, arrival-time and ball-flight primitives
  extras/         standalone BCOS and individual-loss composition helper
  utils/          current shared geometry, action-context and possession utilities
  visualization/  shared native-pitch plots
```

Unused implementations are retained under `archive/legacy_package/`, outside the installed package. The superseded log-linear drive-loss solver and historical choice-model builders/loaders are archived there and are neither exported nor called by the package. The fitted model classes require their current feature contracts; missing or unsupported artifacts raise an error rather than selecting a historical fallback.
